steps.name: environment: install minimal system libs and persist env (idempotent)
steps.description: Install minimal OS libraries required for Chromium headless operation, create and persist a safe /etc/profile.d snippet that sets DISPLAY default only if absent and exports stable PATH and Playwright environment variables (PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS). Use an idempotency marker under /var/local and validate node/npm major versions. Do not run npm inside the root heredoc; compute npm global bin for the current non-root shell and write a runtime-safe snippet. Logs and marker are placed under workspace artifacts.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/native-application-testing-with-playwright-43273/native_application"
ART="$WORKSPACE/artifacts"
mkdir -p "$ART"
LOG="$ART/env_install.log"
MARKER=/var/local/.native_playwright_env_done
# Idempotent marker
if [ ! -f "$MARKER" ]; then
  sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update -q >"$LOG" 2>&1
  sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -yq libgtk-3-0 libgbm1 libnss3 libx11-6 libxcomposite1 libxrandr2 libxss1 libasound2 >"$LOG" 2>&1 || true
  # Prepare profile.d snippet. Compute npm global bin for current user and write a runtime-safe file that only runs npm in interactive shells
  NPM_GBIN=$(npm bin -g 2>/dev/null || echo "/usr/local/bin")
  sudo tee /etc/profile.d/native_playwright_env.sh > /dev/null <<EOF
# persisted by native_application setup
# set default DISPLAY only if not present
export DISPLAY=
DISPLAY=
: "
if [ -z "\${DISPLAY-}" ]; then
  export DISPLAY=":99"
fi
# prepend common global bin and user npm global bin when available
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:${NPM_GBIN}:"]
# Persist Playwright environment defaults
export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="${WORKSPACE}/.local-browsers"
export PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1
# NODE_ENV default for development
export NODE_ENV=development
# Do not force PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD; users can set it externally
EOF
  sudo chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/native_playwright_env.sh
  sudo mkdir -p /var/local && sudo touch "$MARKER"
fi
# Ensure workspace exists
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" "$ART"
# Validate node and npm presence and major versions
if ! command -v node >/dev/null || ! command -v npm >/dev/null; then
  echo "node or npm missing" | tee -a "$LOG" >&2
  exit 2
fi
NODE_VER=$(node -v | sed 's/^v//')
NPM_VER=$(npm -v)
NODE_MAJOR=${NODE_VER%%.*}
NPM_MAJOR=${NPM_VER%%.*}
if [ "$NODE_MAJOR" -lt 18 ]; then echo "node >=18 required, found $NODE_VER" | tee -a "$LOG" >&2; exit 3; fi
if [ "$NPM_MAJOR" -lt 9 ]; then echo "npm >=9 required, found $NPM_VER" | tee -a "$LOG" >&2; exit 4; fi
# Export PATH for current shell to include npm global bin
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:${NPM_GBIN}:$PATH"
# Ensure PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH exists and owned by current user
export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="${WORKSPACE}/.local-browsers"
mkdir -p "$PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH"
sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH" || true

steps.name: dependencies: deterministic npm install, install Chromium, and validate browser
steps.description: Install npm dependencies deterministically (npm ci if package-lock.json exists else npm i), ensure PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH is persisted and owned, run playwright install chromium (prepare script also exists), and validate Chromium using a Node runtime check via Playwright's API. Clean node_modules before npm ci when necessary to avoid mismatch. Capture logs to workspace artifacts and include proxy/network hints on failure.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/native-application-testing-with-playwright-43273/native_application"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
ART="$WORKSPACE/artifacts"
mkdir -p "$ART"
LOG="$ART/install.log"
# Read persisted PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH from profile.d if present, else use workspace default
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="${WORKSPACE}/.local-browsers"
export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH
mkdir -p "$PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH"
sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH" || true
# Persist PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH to /etc/profile.d to ensure future shells see it
sudo sed -i '/PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH/d' /etc/profile.d/native_playwright_env.sh || true
sudo tee -a /etc/profile.d/native_playwright_env.sh > /dev/null <<EOF
export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH"
EOF
sudo chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/native_playwright_env.sh
# Deterministic install: prefer npm ci if lockfile present
if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
  # If node_modules exists from prior non-lockfile install, remove to avoid conflicts
  if [ -d node_modules ] && [ ! -f .npm_ci_succeeded ]; then rm -rf node_modules || true; fi
  npm ci --no-audit --no-fund >"$LOG" 2>&1 || { echo "npm ci failed, see $LOG. If behind proxy set HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY" >&2; tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2; exit 5; }
  touch .npm_ci_succeeded || true
else
  npm i --no-audit --no-fund >"$LOG" 2>&1 || { echo "npm install failed, see $LOG" >&2; tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2; exit 6; }
fi
# Ensure playwright CLI is available locally
if [ ! -x ./node_modules/.bin/playwright ]; then
  echo "playwright CLI missing locally; ensure devDependencies include 'playwright'" >"$ART/playwright_cli_missing.txt"
  exit 7
fi
# Install chromium explicitly (prepare script would run on npm install but ensure here)
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH" ./node_modules/.bin/playwright install chromium >"$ART/playwright_install.log" 2>&1 || { echo "playwright install failed, see $ART/playwright_install.log" >&2; tail -n 200 "$ART/playwright_install.log" >&2; exit 8; }
# Robust validation: use Node + Playwright API to query executable path
node -e "(async()=>{try{const pw=require('playwright');const exe=pw.chromium.executablePath();console.log(exe||'');process.exit(exe?0:11);}catch(e){console.error(e);process.exit(12);}})()" >"$ART/chrome_check.txt" 2>&1 || { echo "Chromium validation failed, see $ART/chrome_check.txt" >&2; tail -n 200 "$ART/chrome_check.txt" >&2; exit 9; }
# Record playwright version
./node_modules/.bin/playwright --version >"$ART/playwright_version.txt" 2>&1 || true

steps.name: testing: run dummy Playwright test (headless) to verify setup and capture artifacts
steps.description: Start the tiny HTTP app, wait for readiness, run Playwright tests using the local playwright binary (explicit path) in headless mode, capture logs and artifacts, and stop the app cleanly. Rely on persisted PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS from /etc/profile.d but export for current run to be explicit. Return test exit code for automation collection.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/native-application-testing-with-playwright-43273/native_application"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
ART="$WORKSPACE/artifacts"
mkdir -p "$ART"
# Use persisted env or defaults
export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="${PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH:-$WORKSPACE/.local-browsers}"
export PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1
# Start app
APP_LOG="$ART/native_app.$(date +%s).log"
node app.js >"$APP_LOG" 2>&1 &
APP_PID=$!
# Wait for port 3000 up with retries (up to 30s)
for i in {1..60}; do curl -sSf http://127.0.0.1:3000/ >/dev/null && break || sleep 0.5; done
if ! curl -sSf http://127.0.0.1:3000/ >/dev/null; then echo "app did not become ready" >&2; tail -n 200 "$APP_LOG" >&2; kill "$APP_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; exit 9; fi
# Run playwright tests using local binary path to avoid npx ambiguity
TEST_LOG="$ART/playwright_test.log"
TEST_RC=0
./node_modules/.bin/playwright test --workers=1 --timeout=30000 >"$TEST_LOG" 2>&1 || TEST_RC=$?
# Stop app
kill "$APP_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
for i in {1..10}; do if ! kill -0 "$APP_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi; sleep 0.5; done
if kill -0 "$APP_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then kill -9 "$APP_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
# Collect evidence
tail -n 200 "$APP_LOG" >"$ART/native_app.last.log" || true
echo "test_exit_code=$TEST_RC" >"$ART/test_exit_code.txt"
exit "$TEST_RC"

# health check (up to 30s)

Scripts follow the required shebang and strict error handling, use the authoritative workspace path, write logs and artifacts into the workspace, and remain non-interactive.
